aboutLead: PXke Algorand is an independent newsroom covering the Algorand blockchain — its markets, protocol, governance, and the projects building on it.
aboutHowBody: Our coverage is assembled automatically from on-chain events, scheduled market data, and monitored community sources, then organised into sections by our editorial pipeline. Every story carries a provenance line so you can trace where it came from.
aboutAiBody: PXke Algorand publishes AI-assisted journalism. Our articles are drafted by AI language models from the on-chain events, market data, and community sources above, under automated editorial review — they are machine-generated rather than written by human reporters. We link to the original sources on every story so you can verify each claim, and the organisation, not an individual byline, is the author of record.
aboutProvenanceBody: On-chain stories are triggered by verifiable transactions and link back to the Algorand explorer. Market stories draw on CoinGecko data. Sponsored placements are always labelled as such and are kept clearly separate from editorial.
aboutStandardsBody: We aim for accuracy and clear attribution. This publication is not investment advice. Spotted an error? Reach out through the source links on any story.
seedsSubtitle: Manually-configured starting points for the crawler. Domains approved from discovery live in the Domains tab.
sourcesDeleteBody: "{serviceId}" will stop being crawled. Articles already published stay.
sourcesRequiredFields: Service id, name and URL are required.
sourcesChangesNextPoll: Changes apply on the next crawler poll.
sourcesMergeIntro: Fold several services into one. The chosen services' sources and domains move to the target; the emptied services are disabled. Use this when one product spans multiple domains (e.g. algorand.co + algorand.com).
sourcesMergeNeedsTwo: Pick a target and at least one service to fold in.
sourcesFieldMatchValueHint: e.g. wallet address or app id
sourcesMatchRuleHelp: The match rule links this source to on-chain activity: when the chain crawler sees a MainNet transaction whose sender/receiver address (kind "address"), application id ("app_id") or asset id ("asset_id") equals the match value, it attributes the event to this source and can trigger an article. For web or Reddit sources it is purely informational — use something descriptive like the domain or subreddit.
domainsIntro: Crawl frontier: domains the link crawler has met. Dead ends are never explored — set automatically by relevance scoring and your review verdicts, or manually here.
domainsEmptyMessage: The crawler records every domain it meets while following links.
domainsPossibleServiceHint: Scored well but tagged news/generic — this may be a real product, not just a citation source. Consider "Full site" instead of "Single page".
